correctness.rationale: The odd divided difference makes the reductions bijective. F(x)−x has valuation one, so F is the identity mod 2 but swaps each parity class mod 4, forcing an even period at every finer level. Exact polynomial multiplication confirms F²(x)−x=8(x²+3x+3)(x²+4x+5), with valuations 3 and 4 on the even and odd classes respectively. All iterates of F² have derivative 1 mod 4. If an iterate H has displacement h of valuation s≥2 then H(H(x))−x=(1+H′(x))h+O(h²) has valuation s+1, since v₂(1+H′(x))=1 and 2s≥s+2. The first returning power of two for F² is the exact least period (which divides that power); doubling it gives the exact F-period at k≥2. Dividing each parity population by its period confirms the cycle counts, including k=1,2,3. The fresh checker verified the identity coefficient by coefficient and the full decompositions through k=14; the lifting proof gives unbounded k.
residual_risks: Finite computation does not replace the exact lifting proof. No classification of other binomial shifts is asserted.

Type II-[s] means split for s levels (each lift has the same length, with twice as many cycles), then grow forever (doubling each length at successive levels).
